title: SDLC event
description: A structured event emitted by the SDLC. The notification subsystem consumes these; it never polls, and it is never the event source. Events are facts about the past, named in the past tense. correlation_id ties every event about one change together, which is what makes a feature thread and an audit trail reconstructable.

id.description: EVT-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-nnnn. Stable, so a duplicate delivery is detectable.

level.description: Mirrors the SDLC hierarchy. Worker-level events are recorded and, by default, not notified.

subject.description: The artifact or work item this is about. Also the default thread key.

actor.description: The agent or human role that caused it. Never a person's name for a worker-level event.

correlates.description: Related artifact ids, so a feature's whole timeline can be reconstructed.

payload.description: Facts only. No prose, no formatting, no recipient list. Routing is the policy engine's job and wording is the agent's.

category.description: Coarse grouping for audit queries and for digest sections.

actor_type.description: What kind of actor caused it. A human actor is a role, never a person's name.

severity.description: The event's own severity, independent of the routing priority the policy assigns.

status.description: Where the thing this event is about now stands.

correlation_id.description: Ties every event about one change together across workflows: the feature id usually, the incident id during an incident. This is what makes a feature thread and an audit trail reconstructable.

artifact.description: The artifact id this event concerns, where it differs from subject.

stage.description: Macro stage id, denormalised from source for querying.

cycle.description: Department cycle id, denormalised from source for querying.
